working: f(x)f(y) = cos(log x)cos(log y). f(x/y)+f(xy) = cos(log x - log y) + cos(log x + log y) = 2 cos(log x)cos(log y), so half of it is exactly f(x)f(y) and the whole expression is 0. Sympy simplifies it to 0 and it evaluates to 0 at the awkward point x=2.7, y=0.31. 0 is not among A(-1), B(1/2), C(-2), so 'none of these' is correct.
subtopic: Functional Equations

working: For an arbitrary even f the equality f(a)=f(b) is guaranteed only when a = b or a = -b. x = (x+1)/(x+2) gives x^2+x-1=0 -> x = 0.6180, -1.6180; x = -(x+1)/(x+2) gives x^2+3x+1=0 -> x = -0.3820, -2.6180. All four lie in [-5,5] and each image (x+1)/(x+2) also lies in [-5,5] (0.618, -1.618, 0.382, 2.618), and none is the excluded x=-2. So 4 values.
subtopic: Domain, Range, and Function Properties

working: Need x-4 >= 0 and 6-x >= 0, i.e. 4 <= x <= 6. The log argument sqrt(x-4)+sqrt(6-x) is strictly positive on that whole interval (both radicals vanish only at x=4 and x=6 respectively, never together; at x=4 it is sqrt(2) and at x=6 it is sqrt(2)). Domain = [4,6].
subtopic: Domain, Range, and Function Properties

working: Set y = (2x-1)/(x+5): y(x+5) = 2x-1 -> x(y-2) = -1-5y -> x = (5y+1)/(2-y). So f inverse (x) = (5x+1)/(2-x), undefined at x=2. Sympy returns (-5y-1)/(y-2), the same thing.
subtopic: Composition and Inverse of Functions
notes: Stem prints the exclusion as (x != 5); the pole of (2x-1)/(x+5) is at x = -5, so the printed restriction is a sign typo in the source. It does not affect the answer.

working: f(1)=f(2)=1 with 1 != 2, so f is not one-to-one. The image is {1,1,0} = {0,1} = Y, so f is onto. Onto but not one-to-one.
subtopic: Function Definition and Classification — Injectivity, Surjectivity, Bijectivity

working: I: f(f(x)) = (1 - (1-x)/(1+x)) / (1 + (1-x)/(1+x)) = (2x)/2 = x, so f is its own inverse -- sympy confirms f(f(x)) = x. II: 5^(log x) = x^(log 5), so f(f(x)) = x^((log 5)^2), and (log 5)^2 = 0.4886 (base 10) or 2.590 (natural), never 1; numerically f(f(3)) = 1.710 != 3. So only I is correct.
subtopic: Composition and Inverse of Functions
notes: Statement II is false for log to any base except base 5 itself, where 5^(log_5 x) = x is the identity map and trivially self-inverse. Judged under the usual base-10/natural reading.

working: t = tan(x/2) gives cos x = (1-t^2)/(1+t^2), dx = 2dt/(1+t^2), and 5+4cos x = (9+t^2)/(1+t^2). The integral becomes 2 dt/(9+t^2) = (2/3) arctan(t/3), so A = 2/3 (and B = 1/3). Differentiating (2/3)arctan((1/3)tan(x/2)) reproduces the integrand exactly at four awkward points, while A=2, 3 and 1/3 all leave a non-zero residual.
subtopic: Integration by Substitution — Algebraic, Trigonometric, and Composite Forms

working: (1+sin x)/(1+cos x) = (1 + 2 sin(x/2)cos(x/2)) / (2cos^2(x/2)) = tan(x/2) + (1/2)sec^2(x/2), which is g + g' with g = tan(x/2). Hence the integral is e^x tan(x/2) + C. Differentiating option A minus the integrand is 0 at x=1.13, while B and C leave residuals 19.44 and 4.13.
subtopic: Standard Forms — Exponential, Logarithmic, and Paired Trigonometric Integrals

working: t = tan(x/2) maps [0, pi/2] to [0,1] and 4+5cos x = (9-t^2)/(1+t^2), so the integral is the integral of 2 dt/(9-t^2) from 0 to 1 = (1/3) ln((3+t)/(3-t)) from 0 to 1 = (1/3) ln 2. Sympy returns log(2)/3 = 0.23105 exactly.
subtopic: Fundamental Theorem, Periodic Integrals, and Leibniz Rule

working: |1-x^2| is even, so the integral is 2 * [ integral 0..1 of (1-x^2) + integral 1..2 of (x^2-1) ] = 2 * [2/3 + 4/3] = 4. Sympy gives 4.
subtopic: Integration of Absolute Value, Piecewise, and Greatest Integer Functions

working: Substituting u = 1-x (King's property on [0,1]) turns it into the integral of (1-u)u^99, = 1/100 - 1/101 = 1/10100. Sympy returns 1/10100.
subtopic: Properties of Definite Integrals — Symmetry, King's, Odd/Even

working: x = sqrt(y) is y = x^2 (x,y >= 0). It meets y = sqrt(x) at (0,0) and (1,1), with sqrt(x) above x^2 in between. Area = integral 0..1 of (sqrt(x) - x^2) = 2/3 - 1/3 = 1/3 sq unit.
subtopic: Area Between Two Curves and Intersection Points

working: For x >= 0, y = |x| = x meets y^2 = x (upper branch y = sqrt(x)) at (0,0) and (1,1); for x < 0 the parabola does not exist, so the only enclosed region is that lens. Area = integral 0..1 of (sqrt(x) - x) = 2/3 - 1/2 = 1/6.
subtopic: Area Between Two Curves and Intersection Points

working: Separable: dy/(1-y) = dx/x^2 -> -ln|1-y| = -1/x + k -> 1-y = A e^(1/x) -> y = 1 + c e^(1/x). Sympy's dsolve returns y = C1*exp(1/x) + 1.
subtopic: Solving and Verifying ODEs — Separable, IVP, and Applications

working: Auxiliary equation m^3 - 4m^2 + 5m - 2 = 0 factors as (m-1)^2 (m-2), so roots are m = 1 (double) and m = 2 (sympy: {2: 1, 1: 2}). General solution = (c1 + c2 x) e^x + c3 e^(2x).
subtopic: Formation of ODE from Curves and General Solutions

working: Highest derivative is d2y/dx2, so order = 2. To read the degree the equation must be made radical-free: sqrt(1 + (y')^2) = -(y'' + 2x y') squares to 1 + (y')^2 = (y'' + 2x y')^2, in which the highest-order derivative y'' appears to the power 2. Order and degree = (2,2).
subtopic: Order, Degree, and Solutions of ODE

working: 1 + sin x sin^2(x/2) = 1 + sin x (1-cos x)/2. The function h(x) = sin x (1-cos x) has h' = 0 at cos x = -1/2, giving extrema +-3 sqrt(3)/4, so the expression is at least 1 - 3 sqrt(3)/8 = 0.3505 > 0 everywhere. Sympy's minimum on [-pi, pi] is 1 - 3 sqrt(3)/8 and a 2,000,001-point scan shows min 0.35048 with zero sign changes, so there are no real solutions. (Equality would need sin x = -1 and sin^2(x/2) = 1 at once, impossible: at x = -pi/2, sin^2(x/2) = 1/2.)
subtopic: General Solutions and Counting Solutions of Trigonometric Equations

working: This is sin(A)cos(B) + cos(A)sin(B) = sin(A+B) with A = 12 deg, B = 78 deg, so it equals sin 90 deg = 1. Numerically 1.0000000.
subtopic: Compound Angle Formulas

working: With A+B+C = 180 deg, (A+B)/2 = 90 - C/2, so tan((A+B)/2) = cot(C/2). Expanding tan((A+B)/2) = (tA + tB)/(1 - tA tB) with tX = tan(X/2) and cross-multiplying gives tA tB + tB tC + tC tA = 1. Checked at the non-symmetric angles A = 0.37 pi, B = 0.41 pi, C = 0.22 pi: sum = 1.0000000.
subtopic: Triangle Identities — A+B+C=π, Half-Angle, and Double-Angle

working: sin 2A + sin 2B = 2 sin(A+B) cos(A-B) = 2 sin C cos(A-B) since A+B = 180 - C, and sin 2C = 2 sin C cos C = -2 sin C cos(A+B). Adding: 2 sin C [cos(A-B) - cos(A+B)] = 4 sin A sin B sin C. Checked at A = 0.37 pi, B = 0.41 pi, C = 0.22 pi: LHS = 2.2470827 = 4 sinA sinB sinC, while 4 cosA cosB cosC = 0.3415 and 2 cosA cosB cosC = 0.1707.
subtopic: Triangle Identities — A+B+C=π, Half-Angle, and Double-Angle
